purpose: Optimize the thin rules layer (one checklist line per iteration) on development tasks only, behind a headroom gate, a two-stage decision, a cost cap against the iteration-0 mean and a researcher that sees only redacted failure classes.

forked_from.relation: Fork of an unfrozen, never-run protocol. The v2 files stay unchanged as an archive. The retarget follows the Claude review stream loop-v2-retarget (findings L1 to L11).
kept_unchanged: equal-size interleaved pairs with adjacent slots

sequencing.enforcement: prepare refuses unless a thin-eval gate record for the chosen model says HEADROOM, the thin-eval freeze exists and binds the same layer v0 bytes, the gate record binds that freeze and the very results file the model selection read (sha256 digests recorded and compared), the model selection record comes from the registered rule, and the campaign root is under the home directory. The machine-wide campaign lock is held for every generation and scoring batch, so no other driver can run and the host stays otherwise idle.
sequencing.gate_rule: HEADROOM only when D shows survival below .95 or fault kill below .95 over its thin-eval cells and the layer was read in at least 90 percent of D cells (the rate every loop decision needs); otherwise NO_HEADROOM or LAYER_NOT_READ and no loop starts.

object.body: Only checklist lines of the form '- [ ] <text>'; no blank lines, headings or fences.
object.edit_grammar: Exactly one checklist line added, deleted, or reworded in place per iteration. A move or any two-line change is refused. Deleting a rule is a legal hypothesis.
object.mount: Identical to thin-eval arm D: read-only /work/skill/thin-rules/SKILL.md plus the D prompt line.
object.d_prompt_line: Read and follow /work/skill/thin-rules/SKILL.md; pass this instruction to the generating child.
object.v0_is_the_baseline: v0 already encodes the id/class selector ban and the no-toHaveClass rule found on dev cells in earlier audits. Those two mechanisms are the baseline, never loop gains; improvements are measured against v0 only.
object.saturation: One rule for both limits: a line can be added only below the 12-line cap and with room for a minimum-size line (40 bytes); a reword or delete stays possible, and a reword may not grow the file once the byte ceiling is reached. The researcher task states each saturation it is under (second-review F10).

arms.loop_arm: D: the official generator (arm A treatment, 19-tool allowlist, auto-approved MCP, danger-full-access) plus the candidate layer. Candidate and incumbent differ only in the mounted file bytes.
arms.reference: A-only reference batch ref-A (six cells by default, ten with the Zeppelin opt-in; no layer) at iteration 0; descriptive.
arms.check_arm: E (D plus the scanner-only gate) is not looped. The final incumbent is compared once against v0 in E during a separate final validation preregistration.

tasks.selection: Dev tasks only. Default list: the synthetic dev split v2-11, v3-08, v2-18 (two repetitions each, six cells per batch). The Zeppelin dev tasks are an opt-in list (see opt_in_hazard). All are disjoint from the six thin-eval tasks and the Zeppelin evaluation pair; the runner never enumerates other task directories and has no final-evaluation command. The staged Zeppelin pool must still contain exactly tasks/zep-sidebar and tasks/zep-note-rename because the shared runtime and its reference calibration use it, but no Zeppelin cell is scheduled by default.
tasks.opt_in_hazard: Opt-in only (prepare --include-zeppelin). The Zeppelin cells use the shared external proxy, so the F3 stale-server hazard (the generation-time test run reuses a server the child's browser exploration already mutated) is NOT repaired there; only the F5 repair applies. They stay out of the default list until a Zeppelin-specific repair is proven live.

model.rule_text: Among Codex candidates with finished thin-eval evidence (at least 12 arm A and 12 arm D cells, results complete; others are skipped and listed with a reason, never ranked), rank by (1) share of arm A and D cells with hard official-tool evidence, (2) delivery share, (3) share of D cells with the layer-read indicator, (4) roster order. Only the fields arm, deliverable, fidelity_class, fidelity.evidence.strength and thin_layer_read_indicator are read; quality, kill, selector, scanner, token, cost and time fields are never read.
model.proposal_note: gpt-6-sol satisfied the superseded arm-C rule and is the lowest-invention candidate, but this offline build could not compute the new rule on the v3 or thin-eval results. The chosen model is whatever select-model records; it is fixed in prepare and bound at freeze.
model.availability: A one-token probe runs inside the machine-wide lock at the start of every generation batch and is retried once. Two failures in a row write BLOCKED.json and end the loop; a rate or usage limit is recorded as RATE_LIMITED, refuses the batch before any cell starts and does not block the campaign. No model is ever substituted.

machinery.single_stack: run-generator-oss-eval-v1.py and the Codex v4 modules it imports. Synthetic and Zeppelin cells are generated, scored and costed through the same module instances; the offline tests prove one engine, evidence and compat instance. The v2 core, v3 runner and thin integration stack are not imported. generator_thin_metrics_v1.py supplies static hygiene counters only.
machinery.freeze_set: Computed, never hand-listed: the static import and path-string closure of the runner and the modules it loads, united with every repository script reachable through the loaded module graph. A test proves every loaded repository script is bound and that an injected unbound module is detected.
machinery.d_staging: stage_layer and d_command mirror thin-eval arm D (an AST parity test compares d_command with the thin-eval source); the layer bytes come from the iteration slot, not from the repository file.
machinery.synthetic_generation: Generation uses the thin-eval-v1 F3 and F5 repairs for the synthetic cells of both D and ref-A: split ports (the MCP session explores on its own port through a server-process-only environment entry; the parent's test run starts a fresh application process, reuseExistingServer false) and git excludes for node_modules and .playwright-mcp/ with the snapshot files kept out of the out-of-scope write check. The repair functions are copied line for line from the thin-eval runner and checked by a syntax-tree parity test. analyze refuses a synthetic cell without the split-port isolation record. Scoring keeps reuseExistingServer false and the v4 scoring guard acts on the same engine instance that scores.
machinery.zeppelin: OSS generate with arm A staging plus the layer mount and D line, cell serials encoded in the repetition so every slot has its own namespace. Only the F5 repair applies (shared external proxy, per-cell note namespaces, no per-session port); the F3 gap is recorded per cell as server_isolation shared-proxy-note-namespace and is an owner decision. Unexercised: the thin-eval Zeppelin amendment is specification only, and the F5 wrapper around the external loop's commit_baseline has never run.
machinery.lock: oss runtime campaign() holds the machine-wide shared lock for each whole batch, synthetic cells included.

baseline.optional_slot: aa3 (owner decides before prepare; recorded in config and bound at freeze)
baseline.schedule: Pairs of (task, repetition) are shuffled with the stage seed; the slots of one pair are adjacent in random order.
baseline.purpose: aa1 and aa2 (D with v0) give the A/A spread and the iteration-0 token means; ref-A is the descriptive official-generator reference.

headroom_gate.rule: LAYER_NOT_READ and stop when the layer was read in fewer than 0.9 of the cells of any D-v0 batch (all 6 of 6 by default, since 5 of 6 is .83; 9 of 10 with the Zeppelin opt-in); otherwise NO_HEADROOM and stop when D-v0 survival is at least .95 and kill over all cells is at least .95 across the aa batches. The NO_HEADROOM stop also applies, and is recorded as no-headroom.json, when an iteration packet has no failing cell. LOW_FIDELITY and stop when any D-v0 batch has a cell that is not official-tool (checked after the layer-read test and before NO_HEADROOM): every later decision requires the official-tool process in both batches of a pair.

iteration.two_stage: A screening pair (incumbent and candidate, one batch each: 6+6 by default, 10+10 with the Zeppelin opt-in) decides first. Only an ADOPT verdict triggers a fresh confirmation pair with its own seed and fresh incumbent cells. Adoption needs ADOPT in both; ADOPT_QUALITY only if both are ADOPT_QUALITY, otherwise ADOPT_COST. A screening ADOPT followed by a confirmation non-adopt is REJECT_ON_CONFIRMATION. Adoption also needs the pooled confirmation gate (decision.pooled_confirmation_gate); a pair that clears both stage tests but not the pooled gate is REJECT_ON_CONFIRMATION.
iteration.history: The incumbent history is every verified batch with the exact incumbent layer sha256 up to the current stage; an adopted candidate's two batches become the next incumbent's A/A history.

decision.primary: dev_refactor_survival: unweighted task mean of binary delivered, clean-3/3 and refactor-pass outcomes; no deliverable or a timeout is zero.
decision.guard_profile_note: strict is the audit's A1 rule (no tolerance) and is the owner's pre-freeze choice of 2026-10-15; prepare defaults to it. noise-tolerant is a registered alternative sized to one cell of clean-rate noise, half a cell of kill noise and about one standard deviation of scanner totals (its tolerances are assumptions); choosing it needs a new owner decision before freeze. No pre-freeze variance measurement is part of this design.
decision.applicability: Layer-read indicator at least 0.9 of the cells (6 of 6 by default; 9 of 10 with the Zeppelin opt-in) in BOTH batches of the pair, else NOT_APPLIED and no credit. The iteration-0 gate enforces the same rate on every D-v0 batch (LAYER_NOT_READ).
decision.cost_path: ADOPT_COST needs survival not lower, a 15 percent reduction in tokens (seconds at most +10 percent) or in seconds (tokens at most +10 percent), and a verification-executed rate not lower than the incumbent's (unknown blocks it).
decision.timeout_scoring: A cell whose last attempt the adapter marks as a wall-clock timeout (not infrastructure) is scored zero and blocks adoption when it occurs in the candidate batch. If its usage is unknown the batch stays analyzable and the cell carries cost_lower_bound true (understated cost can only make a candidate look more expensive against it).
decision.statistics: Every decision reports the exact one-sided task-stratified permutation p (descriptive), the min/max/range of every metric over all incumbent-layer batches, whether the survival delta is within that width, per-task counts and layer bytes. No p-value gates adoption.

guard_profile_decision.reason: A low false-adopt rate is preferred to missing a real improvement, because a false adoption stacked on a tiny rules file is the main risk. noise-tolerant stays registered but is not chosen.

adoption_requirements.official_tool_fidelity: Every cell of the candidate batch AND of the incumbent batch it is compared with has fidelity class official-tool (the thin-eval arm A/D classifier). A cell with another class or none counts as not official. Failing it is a REJECT on either adoption path (second-review F1).
adoption_requirements.no_task_regression: For every active task the candidate's survival count is at least the incumbent's, on both the quality and the cost path (second-review F4): one cell moves the three-task mean by .17, so a net +1 cell must not hide a regressed task.

decision.pooled_confirmation_gate: After both stages ADOPT, screening and confirmation are pooled (twelve cells per arm by default, twenty with the opt-in): the cells must be disjoint (recorded call IDs), no task may be lower for the candidate, and on the quality path the pooled net gain must be at least 3 cells (.25 of the pooled mean by default, .15 with the opt-in). Failing it is REJECT_ON_CONFIRMATION. The confirmation still re-runs the same development tasks (fresh cells, not fresh tasks); the stricter pooled threshold is the stated compensation, not a cure.

cost.tokens: Processed tokens per cell: uncached input plus output over every attempt, parent and verified children. Cached input is reported separately and enters the cached-inclusive checks.
checks: processed vs the iteration-0 D mean
cached-inclusive vs the iteration-0 D mean
cost.layer_text_cost_note: The layer is about 470 estimated tokens against 100k+ per cell; the real cost risk is behavioural (extra turns), which the token checks measure.
cost.overhead: Researcher usage and seconds are recorded beside, never inside, generation efficiency; unknown usage is recorded as unknown.

precedence: layer ceiling without a valid shrinking candidate
stop.valid_null_result: No adopted change, keep v0, is a valid recorded outcome.
stop.void_budget_rule: Void cells count toward the generation budget: a void stage is charged the cells it started (recorded in VOID.json; its whole schedule when unknown), an archived void stays charged, and a retry must still fit the remaining budget. A killed process that left a started stage without a verdict is charged its whole schedule.
stop.retry_rule: retry-void archives an infrastructure void (retryable true, written only for an adapter-reported infrastructure failure) that was never completed, scored or analyzed, writes a ledger entry and lets the same deterministic schedule run again. Integrity stops (input drift, candidate change, namespace violation) and score voids are never retryable. No cell content is read, the voided cells never enter a decision, a packet or a noise estimate, and the retry count is bounded.

researcher.default: A Claude subagent invoked by the owner in the staged workspace; any other command may be plugged in with researcher-run, which refuses Codex and records the identity.
researcher.input: workspace/{TASK.md, incumbent/THIN-RULES.md, packet.json, optional library/ with the three public product reference files}, in a private temporary directory outside the campaign tree (recorded in staged.json). No repository, campaign, task truth, raw literals, forbidden-token file, call IDs or case names. Isolation is by location and instruction only (HOME is kept, no filesystem sandbox).
researcher.output: out/{THIN-RULES.md, hypothesis.json, hypothesis.md}; one diff per iteration; the exact bytes written are preserved in the draw as researcher-out.

draws.rule: Both draws are preserved; an invalid draw is not redone; two spent draws without an accepted candidate is NO_CANDIDATE, a non-adoption.

researcher.redaction: Deterministic: outcome flags, closed-vocabulary error classes (strict_mode_violation, locator_wait_timeout, assertion_mismatch, ...), static hygiene counters, task labels T1..T5, opaque cell references, and a skeleton of at most three failing specs with every literal and unknown identifier replaced.
researcher.failure_rule: A cell is failing if it is not delivered, timed out, not clean 3/3, failed the refactor, has kill rate below 0.8, or did not use the official generator surface (fidelity class other than official-tool).
researcher.wording_screen: Forbidden phrases, selector or identifier tokens, application vocabulary and task ids are derived from the raw packet evidence (spec literals, identifiers, error text, plan behaviors) minus a generic vocabulary built from words that occur at least 3 times in the three public product reference files plus the incumbent's own words; a fixed grader-vocabulary ban (refactor, restyle, rename, markup, grader, scorer, mutant, held-out, benchmark, eval, evals, evaluation) always applies. Violations are reported by category, never by token. Second review (F7): the screen also sees through separators and punctuation inside a word, spaced-out letters and squashed spellings; the grader list is widened (oracle, rubric, score, grade, hidden test, reference solution, fault, injected, kill rate, survival, calibration). Still a screen, not a proof: paraphrase and a smuggled instruction in general words are not detectable offline.
researcher.semantic_review: An independent Claude-family reviewer other than the researcher session and other than the generating model records the exact prompt, output, diff digest and verdict; prompt and output digests are checked and the prompt is recomputed.
researcher.repository_review: scripts/ci/review.sh on a disposable tracked checkout with the candidate overlaid on the layer path. Weak by construction: review.sh does not inspect the layer text; the grammar, the derived wording screen and the wording review carry the real load.
researcher.static_stage: See static_stage: an offline, pre-registered screen of the added line before any live cell.

integrity.freeze: Not created by this build. Freeze binds protocol, README, tests, the computed script closure, layer v0, the baseline copy, the library files, model selection, thin-eval gate, plans, schedules and DEV task bytes, and requires an independent-review.json that records a PASS for the exact runner, protocol, README and tests from a reviewer other than the builder.
integrity.independent_review: Open. The first independent review (R1 to R9) found material problems that this revision repairs; its PASS, if any, does not cover the repaired bytes. No freeze, calibration or live command works until a different reviewer records PASS for the exact runner, protocol, README and tests (finding L1). Record format: JSON {verdict: PASS, open_material_findings: 0, reviewer: {id, model}, builder: {id, model} (different ids and models), reviewed_sha256: {runner, protocol, readme, tests}}.
integrity.outputs: Exclusive and append-only; interrupted or infrastructure-invalid batches are VOID and cannot decide. A void stage is archived, never rerun in place (retry-void).
integrity.candidate: The candidate layer, hypothesis, diff, packet, reviews and researcher record are re-validated before and during every batch.

runtime.source: The current OSS protocol's immutable container image, 1500-second call timeout, disk floor, load pause and shared campaign lock; one operation at a time.
runtime.no_substitution: No model switching, dependency installation, implicit build, commit or push.

decision_simulation.design: Per replicate: three task survival probabilities (the default synthetic dev split; the opt-in five-task table is results_with_zeppelin_opt_in) from a logit-normal (sd .6) around the base; clean .92; kill in {.6,.8,1} with weights {.2,.3,.5} when clean; scanner P0 Poisson .15 and P1/P2 Poisson 1.2 per cell; processed tokens lognormal sd .15 around 100k; cached 400k; layer read .97; the candidate differs only by a constant survival shift. Up to six iterations with the real stop rule and the full two-stage decision, 2000 replicates, seed 20261017. Revised after the second review (F1, F4): every simulated cell is official-tool, a task regression blocks adoption, and a pair that clears both stages must also clear the pooled gate (net gain of at least 3 cells); the published results were regenerated with the revised rule.
decision_simulation.reading: Under these assumed noise levels the strict profile almost never adopts, even a true +.2 effect: P(iteration adopts)=0.0015 and P(loop adopts at least once)=0.003 (the review's roughly 0.004 was the earlier figure; the added task-regression and pooled gates lower it slightly). The noise-tolerant profile adopts a true +.2 effect in about 1.5 percent of iterations (2.9 percent of loops). The guard design, not the stage count, dominates the power. A loop that adopts nothing costs at least 42 Codex cells by default before it stops (70 with the opt-in). The loop is therefore a near-certain 'keep v0' under strict; this is stated as the expected outcome, not hidden.

findings_addressed.L1: Open by design: freeze requires a recorded independent PASS review of the exact files.
findings_addressed.L2: Single stack, computed freeze closure, same-instance guards, tests.
findings_addressed.L3: Two-stage decision, six iterations, optional third A/A batch, published offline simulation, guard profiles.
findings_addressed.L4: Cumulative and cached-inclusive caps, byte and growth caps, slow-cell guard.
findings_addressed.L5: Packet-derived forbidden-token screen, grader vocabulary ban, reviewer identity and artifacts.
findings_addressed.L6: Literal-redacted packet with deterministic failure classes; v0 is the baseline.
findings_addressed.L7: Outcome-blind arm A/D model rule and per-batch availability probe ending the loop as BLOCKED.
findings_addressed.L8: Sequencing gate and the machine-wide lock held per batch.
findings_addressed.L9: NO_CANDIDATE verdict and two preserved draws.
findings_addressed.L10: Timeouts scored zero and separated from infrastructure; no-op researcher smoke listed as a first-live check.
findings_addressed.L11: Pool guard accepts only a staged DEV-only copy.

limits: Five reused development tasks, two repetitions; one cell moves survival .10. Adaptive reuse can overfit and nothing here is an unseen-task, sealed, release or cross-model claim.
The two Zeppelin tasks share an application and one upstream change.
The decision simulation uses assumed, not measured, noise.

No model, browser, Docker, server, Zeppelin or network behaviour was exercised: availability probe, layer mount, child instruction receipt, token accounting, Zeppelin D cells, researcher command and the unexercised live path are all unverified.
A final validation of the winning layer needs a separate preregistration on tasks never used by any campaign and at least one other model.
The synthetic dev tasks use one-paragraph truth-derived plans, not curated multi-behavior plans; the loop's D cells are not thin-eval-comparable.
The two Zeppelin dev tasks have no F3 repair (shared proxy, note namespaces); they receive F5 only.

review_repairs.R1: Synthetic D and ref-A cells carry the thin-eval F3 split-port and F5 git-exclude repairs (copied functions, syntax-tree parity, real git test); Zeppelin gets F5 only, F3 gap is an owner decision.
review_repairs.R2: Synthetic record carries the OSS arm; a test feeds a record from the real synthetic_generate to the real cell_extras, rollout_summary, cell_tokens and indicators.
review_repairs.R3: Iteration-0 gate requires 9 of 10 layer reads in every D-v0 batch (LAYER_NOT_READ stop); thin-eval gate threshold aligned to 90 percent.
review_repairs.R4: No default guard profile, no pre-freeze variance step, expected spend and near-null outcome stated; the choice stays an owner decision.
review_repairs.R5: Researcher workspace outside the campaign tree, outputs preserved, claims reworded.
review_repairs.R6: Disclosed: one-paragraph plans for the synthetic dev tasks.
review_repairs.R7: Unfinished models skipped and listed; finished thin-eval D cells required; gate record carries and prepare verifies results and freeze digests.
review_repairs.R8: Probe retry and rate-limit separation; lower-bound cost for timed-out cells; slot-blind adjudication documented; campaign root under home; packet-time NO_HEADROOM recorded.
review_repairs.R9: Grader pattern narrowed, control characters rejected, unused import removed, review record format documented; test is run directly like its siblings.

owner_decisions.decision: Guard profile STRICT. A low false-adopt rate is preferred to missing a real improvement, because a false adoption stacked on a tiny rules file is the main risk. Recorded as a pre-freeze decision; prepare defaults to strict.

Dev tasks are the synthetic dev split only at first (v2-11, v3-08, v2-18). The Zeppelin dev tasks zep-sidebar and zep-note-rename are dropped from the default task list and kept as an opt-in list (prepare --include-zeppelin) with the shared-proxy F3 hazard disclosed, until a Zeppelin-specific repair is proven. Recorded as a pre-freeze decision.

static_stage.status: offline, deterministic, pre-registered; runs at researcher ingest and again at candidate validation, before any of the live cells
static_stage.why_not_the_scanner: The e2e-reviewer scanner reads specs, not rule text, so running it on fixed reference specs 'under the candidate rules' would not depend on the candidate. The stage instead screens the added line against the scanner's own anti-pattern vocabulary (waitForTimeout, networkidle, force clicks, test.only/skip, error swallowing, vacuous assertions, raw DOM queries, class assertions, positional locators) and against risky-action wording.
static_stage.flagged_pattern_rule: A scanner-flagged pattern may be named only to forbid it (a negation precedes it in its clause) or under 'only with/when/if/after', 'unless' or a JUSTIFIED marker.
static_stage.risky_actions: Install or download, network access, credential or secret use, a write outside the generated tests or a destructive command, and skipping or bypassing the official generator and its tools. Categories only are reported.
static_stage.limits: A fixed-pattern screen cannot see a paraphrase; it lowers the rate of obviously risky or malformed candidates and saves live cells, nothing more. The independent wording review and the fidelity requirement remain.

calibration.rule: The calibration file must hold a passing record for exactly the active mode's tasks (second-review F2): the three synthetic tasks by default, those plus the two Zeppelin tasks with the opt-in.
calibration.synthetic: Offline and model-free: every registered fault edit applies exactly once to the case application, every fault yields a distinct mutant that differs from the clean app, and the refactor edits apply and change it. The synthetic tasks ship no reference spec, so there is no reference run; that a good spec kills each mutant remains a live check (live_reference_run is recorded false).
calibration.zeppelin: With the opt-in only: the existing reference-spec calibration through the shared scoring path, merged into the same file.

matches.d_prompt_line: The D prompt line is byte-identical to thin-eval's (prepare refuses otherwise; an offline test compares them).
matches.layer_mount: Read-only nested bind mount at /work/skill/thin-rules/SKILL.md (d_command compared with the thin-eval source).
matches.tool_allowlist: The official generator surface (arm A treatment, 19-tool allowlist, auto-approved MCP) is the shared one.

mismatches.plans: Synthetic dev tasks use one-paragraph truth-derived plans (a single Behavior 1), not the curated multi-behavior plans of thin-eval's synthetic tasks. Not fixed: curated plans for the dev tasks do not exist and writing them is outside this build.
mismatches.entry_check: thin-eval requires at least 18 of 24 jointly qualifying D cells (official-tool plus layer-read). The loop's entry gate now requires, per D-v0 batch, the layer-read rate (0.9) and, since the second review, an official-tool rate of 1.0 (LOW_FIDELITY); the joint per-cell condition is covered by decide() requiring both.
mismatches.endpoints: thin-eval reports selector hygiene, clean-conditional survival, unconditional refactor score, clean, effective fault kill, per-model pooled and intention-to-treat versus as-treated views, and processed/cached token ratios against comparators. The loop decides on dev refactor survival with guards (clean, kill, scanner, timeouts, tokens) as intention-to-treat on all cells with a layer-read applicability gate; selector hygiene is descriptive only, and there is one model.
mismatches.tasks_and_repetitions: thin-eval: six tasks, 24 cells per arm per model. Loop: three dev tasks (five with the opt-in), six cells per batch.
mismatches.models_and_arms: thin-eval compares seven arms across a roster. The loop compares two D batches (candidate layer versus incumbent layer) on one model; A is a descriptive reference batch at iteration 0 only.
mismatches.fidelity_gate: thin-eval classifies fidelity per cell and gates its sufficiency statement on it. The loop's decide() did not read the class (second-review F1); it now requires official-tool for every cell of both batches. The classifier is the shared one, so its evidence limits (a parent-stream indicator, child-only reads missed) apply.

limits_second_review.low_power: Under the assumed noise the default strict profile adopts a true +.2 improvement with P(iteration)=0.0015 and P(loop at least once)=0.003; the noise-tolerant profile 0.0149 and 0.029. One cell moves a three-task mean by .17. The loop is a near-certain 'keep v0' and its main product is an honest null; it cannot detect small effects, and no outcome here is a significance, release or generalization claim.
limits_second_review.redaction_limits: The skeleton redaction is not a privacy boundary. It keeps statement order, Playwright API names, numbers, kind tags for every literal (css-id, css-class, css-attribute, text), regular-expression and template-literal markers, and every identifier of at most four letters, so the sequence of user steps, the locator strategy, counts and timeouts and short application words (for example a four-letter noun) can survive. It also truncates at 2500 characters. The forbidden-token screen is derived from the raw evidence and catches echoes, not a paraphrase of the structure. The packet therefore leaks the shape of failing tests by design (that is its use); only literals and long identifiers are removed.
limits_second_review.scorer_calibration: The synthetic calibration is an applicability check of the mutants, not a reference-spec run.
limits_second_review.void_retry: Score voids and integrity voids are terminal; a hand-written VOID.json is outside what offline code can prevent (the retry only verifies the partial-record digests recorded at void time).
limits_second_review.zeppelin_retry: With the opt-in, a retry reuses the cell serials and so the note namespaces; a namespace that retains notes from the voided cells would produce a namespace violation, which is not retryable. Unexercised live.

second_review_repairs.F1: Repaired: decide() requires official-tool fidelity for every cell of the candidate and incumbent batches; failing() counts a non-official cell as failing; the entry gate adds LOW_FIDELITY.
second_review_repairs.F2: Repaired: calibration covers the active mode's tasks; a synthetic offline calibration was added and the calibrate command writes it (Zeppelin reference calibration only with the opt-in).
second_review_repairs.F3: Repaired: void cells are charged to the budget; a bounded, recorded retry-void path for infrastructure voids; no result peeking.
second_review_repairs.F4: Repaired: no per-task regression on both paths and a pooled confirmation gate with disjoint cells and a stricter threshold; the same-tasks limitation is stated, not removed.
second_review_repairs.F5: Repaired: an offline static inner stage before any live cell (the scanner itself is not meaningful on rule text, see static_stage).
second_review_repairs.F6: Documented: low power stated with the regenerated numbers (limits_second_review.low_power).
second_review_repairs.F7: Repaired as far as is sound: separator, punctuation and spaced-letter evasions, a wider grader list and a risky-action screen; paraphrase remains undetectable.
second_review_repairs.F9: Documented plus the cheap fixes: the entry check now includes the official-tool rate; remaining mismatches are listed in thin_eval_alignment.
second_review_repairs.F10: Repaired: one saturation rule for bytes and line count (add_possible, saturation_notice), told to the researcher and recorded in NO_CANDIDATE.
